investigation.title: Remote Agents: Swarm Gateway 502 — All Three Remote-Agent Checks Failing with Identical Bad-Gateway Error
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-09-14T20:57:13–46Z with an identical 502 bad-gateway error indicating the swarm provisioning gateway (an AWS ELB in us-east-2) was unreachable when POST /api/agents was called. Because the failure is identical across all sibling checks and no evidence was collected, the root cause is localized to the shared upstream swarm gateway dependency, not to any individual check's logic.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm gateway — the AWS ELB endpoint that backs POST /api/agents at the /v1/agents path — was unreachable at the time of the eval run. The production-api layer returned HTTP 502 with code "bad_gateway" and the message "swarm gateway unreachable during agent provisioning: error sending request for url (http://[REDACTED].elb.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/v1/agents)" for every remote-agent check. Because all three sibling checks share the same upstream dependency (the swarm gateway) and all returned the exact same error message within a 33-second window, the failure is a shared infrastructure dependency failure, not a per-check code defect. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected by any check, confirming the gateway was never reached successfully. This is an eval-detected infrastructure availability issue; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact to production users cannot be confirmed from this packet alone.

investigation.summary: The image-generation-stream eval failed because the OpenAI API key used by the eval runner has no remaining credits, causing the upstream image generation call to be rejected with error code credit_balance_exhausted. The eval infrastructure correctly detected and surfaced the upstream error; the contract assertions failed as a direct downstream consequence of the quota exhaustion, not because of a logic bug in the runner or a misconfigured contract.

investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-runtime, remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state) failed at 2026-09-14T20:57 with an identical 502 bad_gateway error: the production-api layer could not reach the swarm ELB endpoint at /v1/agents during agent provisioning. investigations.rootCause: The swarm gateway — the AWS ELB-backed service at the redacted us-east-2 endpoint that handles POST /v1/agents — was unreachable from the production-api layer at the time of the eval run. Every call to POST /api/agents was proxied through this gateway and returned HTTP 502 with error code bad_gateway and the message "swarm gateway unreachable during agent provisioning." Because agent creation is the first step in all three remote-agents checks (confirmed by the runner calling createAgent at run-status-probes.mjs:1918), none of the checks could proceed past provisioning, and no evidence (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) was collected.
